newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China says its troops symbolise sovereignty in HK.
newsitem.headline: China says its troops symbolise sovereignty in HK.

text.p: China said on Monday its troops in Hong Kong were a small symbol of sovereignty over the territory, and internal security would be left to local police.

Some Western leaders and pro-democracy campaigners in Hong Kong have expressed fears about the new garrison's role, saying its mass arrival in hours surrounding the territory's handover would create unease.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said: "The stationing of troops in Hong Kong is a symbol of China's resumption of (the) exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong."
"As for the internal security of Hong Kong, that will be the responsibility of the police of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government," he told a news conference.
Beijing will send 509 soldiers into Hong Kong on Monday night, three hours before the British colony's midnight (1600 gmt) reversion to Chinese rule.

A second wave of 4,000 will arrive by land, sea and air around dawn on Tuesday, backed by ships, helicopters and armoured personnel carriers. The speed and size of their deployment has raised concern in the territory and abroad.
The question of the troops' arrival had been raised by the foreign ministers of several nations during bilateral meetings on Monday with China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, Shen said.
The foreign ministers indicated they understood the issue better after being briefed by Qian, he added.
Shen also said the Chinese garrison was much smaller than the British military's past presence.

"In some periods of time the British troops have amounted to 30 to 40,000, and the British troops also had armoured (personnel) carriers. So in comparison to this, China's troops to Hong Kong is much much less," he said.
Britain briefly had a sizeable force stationed in Hong Kong following the end of World War Two, guarding Hong Kong against a spill over from the ongoing Chinese civil war.
After that some 10,000 troops were stationed in the colony to guard the border, but in recent months the number of British troops has dwindled to fewer than 1,000.
Shen also said Britain had some 23 or 24 barracks in Hong Kong, but that the Chinese garrison would only have 14.
As part of the handover of British military lands in Hong KOng, China agreed to let the future Special Administrative Region government take over land the People's Liberation Army did not need.
